messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a ~15-25% tail-latency regression on decode for medium-length requests (200-600 tokens) after the kernel-selector change last week. Repro on prod and a small staging pool.

sam: :eyes: which selector/heuristic triggered it?

maria: The autotuner started preferring the matmul-fused-decode path for these sizes on A100s when sequence len distribution is mixed. Previously it used the hybrid-attn path. Perf diff shows larger kernel launch overhead + less effective kv cache streaming.

jess: Can you paste the profiling snippet? NVTX or perf?

maria: Pasted quick flame: `decode_total` jumps at about 180 tokens. NVPROF shows 2x more small kernel launches (reduce + reorder) vs hybrid. profiler-bot: upload complete -> s3://redwood-prof/1782345678/prof.zip

mike: I can repro locally on a small A100 node with batch=4. Looks like batching heuristics also changed: continuous-batcher is grouping by arrival rather than sequence length, so mixed-length batches surface the less-efficient path.

jess: That explains it — matmul-fused benefits when sequences are long or uniform. Mixed medium + short will thrash kv cache placement and increase decode overhead.

sam: Quick mitigation idea: lower threshold for the matmul path for architectures where launch overhead dominates (A100/T4) until autotuner gathers more samples. Or add a micro-benchmark step in the selector that tests with current seq-distribution.

maria: Agreed. I sketched a config tweak:

```
# temp heuristic
kernel_picker:
  matmul_threshold: 800    # revert from 256 -> 800 for matmul path
  hybrid_prefer_window: 128
  autotune_sample_count: 500
```

mike: That seems backward — increasing matmul_threshold will pick matmul for larger sequences only. We want matmul disabled for medium mixed loads. Maybe set `matmul_max_for_mixed: 128` and use `path_override_for_mixed=true`

jess: Another approach: add a per-batch composition check in the continuous-batcher. If variance(seq_len) > X, force hybrid path. Cheap check: track running mean and stddev for the batch.

maria: Yeah I prototyped that: if stddev/mean > 0.25 then route to hybrid. Microbench gave ~12% improvement on our repro harness.

sam: Sounds promising. How about autotuner changes: sample on representative mixed batches and expose a safety margin so selector doesn't flip for small delta perf. Autotune should report confidence intervals, not just a single number.

mike: Also KV layout mattered — I saw more cache misses when we used the compacted kv buffer layout with matmul path. Hybrid does streaming-friendly offsets. Could we revert kv layout change for decode path only?

maria: Reverting KV layout for decode could be low-risk. Plan: 1) patch batcher to check variance and force hybrid for mixed batches, 2) revert kv-layout change for decode path, 3) run autotune with `window=2000` and CI reporting, 4) monitor canary.

jess: +1. Can we ship a small rolling canary tomorrow? I can put together the rollout config (canary=5%, region=us-west-2, model=redwood-v2)

sam: I'll modify autotuner to emit a JSON summary with mean/std/confidence so ops can decide. Example: `{"path":"matmul", "latency_ms": 34.2, "ci95": [32.1,36.3], "samples": 120}`

infra-bot: deploy triggered by sam -> deploy/job/1782345690 (staging small canary).

profiler-bot: autotune run started (id=autotune-1782345701)

mike: After the patch I repro'd baseline perf on staging. We'll still need to watch long-tail under peak load.

maria: Created PR with batcher variance check + kv layout revert: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1426. Added test harness script to feed mixed distributions.

jess: Nice. Add a regression test that simulates mixed arrival patterns so autotune doesn't flip back.

maria: Will do. Also adding a flag `selector.safety_margin_pct` default=5 to require at least X% improvement before switching paths.

sam: Great. Let's ship the canary tonight and keep an eye on token-level latency dashboards. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
